extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent agents and attorneys) practicing before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing ethical conduct, disclosure, consent, business dealings, and remedial obligations for practitioners (agents/attorneys) registered to practice before the USPTO, as reflected in a USPTO Final Order imposing discipline. Includes specific regulatory citations, required actions, and sanctions/procedures for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner subject to USPTO Disciplinary Rules / USPTO jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times relevant hereto, Respondent ... has been an agent registered to practice patent law before the Office (Registration No. 58,188) and is subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq. The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners are covered by 37 C.F.R. §10.20 et seq.; disciplinary actions are within the Director's statutory/regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. §2(b)(2)(D); 37 C.F.R. §11.26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of potential or actual conflicts arising from practitioner's being a co-inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to accepting employment to represent the client before the Office, Respondent did not disclose the potential or actual conflict of interests that could arise between him and the client if Respondent were named as an inventor on a patent application seeking patent protection for inventions similar to, or derivative of, the client's invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must disclose potential/actual conflicts that could arise from being named as a co-inventor before accepting employment; failure to disclose may violate USPTO disciplinary rules. The Final Order treats such nondisclosure as sanctionable conduct whether or not intentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain client's consent after full disclosure when practitioner's personal interests may affect professional judgment (37 C.F.R. §10.62(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.62(a) — accepting employment as a patent agent without obtaining the client's consent after full disclosure where the exercise of Respondent's professional judgment on behalf of the client will be or reasonably may be affected by Respondent's own financial, business, property, or personal interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before accepting employment that could create a conflict, the practitioner must fully disclose the conflict and obtain the client's informed consent; failing to do so is a violation of §10.62(a). The Order clarifies that lack of intent does not necessarily excuse the failure to obtain consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of potential or actual conflicts arising from contracting with client to assist in development/marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent did not disclose the potential or actual conflict of interests that could arise between Respondent and the client as a result of Respondent also being hired to assist the client in developing and marketing the client's valve clip invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a practitioner enters a business relationship to develop/design/assemble/manufacture/market a client's invention, the practitioner must disclose potential conflicts such a relationship creates and obtain the client's consent after full disclosure. Failure to disclose is sanctionable even if the client had independent counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not enter into business transactions with a client without consent after full disclosure (37 C.F.R. §10.65)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.65 — entering into a business transaction with the client to develop, design, assemble, manufacture, and market the client's invention without obtaining the client's consent after full disclosure where the client and Respondent could have differing interests therein and where the client might have expected Respondent to exercise professional judgment therein for the protection of the client's interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must avoid business transactions with clients that create differing interests unless the practitioner fully discloses the conflict and the client gives informed consent. Failure to obtain consent is a violation of §10.65 and may lead to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming oneself (but not the client) as inventor while prosecuting client's applications creates conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent created a potential or actual conflict of interest with the client by naming himself, but not the client, as an inventor in Applications ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming the practitioner as an inventor on applications prosecuted for a client can create an actual or potential conflict of interest; such situations require disclosure and informed client consent before representation and related filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of applications to client / duty to assist in obtaining assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty (30) days from the date this Final Order is signed, Respondent shall assign, or cause to be assigned, to the client ... the following applications: U.S. Provisional Application No. ..., Non-Provisional Patent Application No. ..., and ... With respect to U.S. Non-Provisional Patent Application No. ..., within thirty (30) days ... Respondent shall assign to, cause to be assigned to, or provide reasonable assistance in obtaining an assignment (or assignments) for the benefit of the client ... and, in the event the application has not yet been assigned, Respondent shall be under a continuing duty to provide reasonable assistance obtaining such assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When ordered by the Office, practitioners must execute assignments or otherwise reasonably assist clients in obtaining assignments within the required timeframes; the duty to assist may be ongoing until assignment is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide copies of Final Order to client and inventors and file affidavits attesting compliance within specified timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty (30) days from the date this Final Order is signed, Respondent shall provide a copy of this Final Order to the client ... Within forty-five (45) days ... Respondent shall provide the OED Director an affidavit attesting to compliance ... Within thirty (30) days ... Respondent shall provide a copy of this Final Order to the inventors identified in U.S. Patent Application Nos. ... Within forty-five (45) days ... Respondent shall provide the OED Director an affidavit attesting to compliance ... and the documentation evidencing his compliance (e.g., a copy of the correspondence to the inventors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order imposes concrete deadlines (30 and 45 days) for notifying affected parties and delivering sworn attestations and supporting documentation to OED; compliance is tracked and enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions: public reprimand; probation; suspension process and enforcement procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent be, and hereby is, publicly reprimanded; Respondent shall serve a twenty-four (24) month probationary period ... In the event that the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent, during the probationary period, failed to comply with any provision of this Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule ..., the OED Director shall: (1) issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause ... grant Respondent fifteen days to respond ... (2) if OED continues to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply ... deliver to the USPTO Director ... and request that the USPTO Director immediately suspend Respondent for up to twenty-four (24) months ... any such review of the suspension shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions include public reprimand and probation; noncompliance triggers an Order to Show Cause with a 15-day response window and may lead to immediate suspension up to 24 months. Requests for review do not stay suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of suspension regarding USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended: (1) the USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and Public Key Infrastructure ('PKI') certificates; (2) Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO; and (3) Respondent may not obtain a USPTO customer number or a PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension entails immediate disassociation from USPTO electronic credentials and a prohibition on use or re-obtainment until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing legal education / remedial ethics training
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent represents that, since the events at issue, he has enrolled and completed a continuing legal education course entitled 'Legal Ethics 2011' sponsored by the State Bar of Wisconsin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of ethics CLE may be used as remedial or mitigating evidence in disciplinary contexts; the Order records such completion as part of the stipulated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice (with limited redactions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room ... except that the names of the inventors ... and all application numbers referenced herein shall be redacted; The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with attached Exhibit A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary orders are made public with certain redactions for privacy; publication serves notice and institutional record-keeping purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may use record of proceeding in future disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or this Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including this Final Order, when (1) addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning Respondent brought to the attention of the Office, and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding concerning Respondent (i) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's prior disciplinary record may be used as aggravation or rebuttal in future proceedings; compliance history matters for future sanctions.
